chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah al-Hāshimī, from ʿAlī ibn Muhammad or Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī, who said:

I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) on the morning of his wedding, when he had consummated with al-Maʾmūn’s daughter. I had taken some medicine during the night, so I was the first to enter upon him that morning. Thirst had afflicted me, and I disliked to ask for water. Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) looked at my face and said, “I think you are thirsty.” I said, “Yes.” So he said, “O boy, or girl, give us water to drink.”

So I said to myself, “At this very moment they will bring him water in which they will poison him,” and I became distressed because of that. Then the servant came with the water, and he smiled at my face, then said, “O boy, hand me the water.” So he took the water and drank, then handed it to me, and I drank. Then I became thirsty again and disliked to ask for water, so he did as he had done the first time. When the servant came with the cup, I said to myself the like of what I had said the first time. So he took the cup, then drank, then handed it to me, and smiled.
Muhammad ibn Hamzah said: This Hāshimī said to me, “And I think that he is as they say.”

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the Imam mentioned in the narration
key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيُّ: the Hāshimī narrator or informant mentioned at the end

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the insight and spiritual rank of Imām Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an incident from the morning after the marriage of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), in which he perceived the unspoken thirst and inner thoughts of a visitor. The report serves as a biographical and theological indication of the Imam’s exceptional awareness and supports the belief of the narrator in the Imam’s rank.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Hamza Al Hashimy, from Ali Bin Muhammad or Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hashimy who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> on the morning of his<sup>asws</sup> marriage when he<sup>asws</sup> married the daughter of Al-Mamoun, and I had taken medicine the night before. So the first one to go over to him in the morning was me, and the thirst had hit me, and I disliked to call for the water. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> (9<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) looked at me in my face and said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> think you are thirsty. So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O boy! or ‘O Maid! Quench us with the water’.

So I said within myself, ‘At this time he would come with the water having been poisoned with’, and I was gloomy due to that. So the boy came and with him was the water, and he<sup>asws</sup> smiled in my face, then said: ‘O boy! Give me<sup>asws</sup> the water!’. So he gave him<sup>asws</sup> the water, and he<sup>asws</sup> drank’. Then he gave it to me, so I drank. Then I was thirsty as well, and I disliked to call for the water. So he<sup>asws</sup> did what he<sup>asws</sup> had done formerly. So when the boy came and with him was the cup, I said within myself the like of what I had said during the first (time). So he<sup>asws</sup> took the cup and drank, then he<sup>asws</sup> gave it to me and smiled’.
Muhammad Bin Hamza said, ‘So this Hashimy said to me, ‘And I think he<sup>asws</sup> is just as they (Shias) are saying’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn zd from Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja‘fari who has said the following “Once I went to see abu Ja‘far (a.s.) and I had a few questions on three pieces of materials with proper markings and they were mixed as such that I could not distinguish. I felt sad. He picked one and said, “This is the letter of Ziyad ibn Shabib.” Then he picked up the other one and said, “.This is the letter of so and so.” I became awe struck.

He looked at me and smiled.” The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) then gave me three hundred Dinars and asked me to deliver them to the certain persons of the sons of his uncle and said, “He will ask you to show him a professional person who would help him to buy goods, help show him one.” The narrator has said that I then went to him and gave him the Dinars and asked me, “O abu Hashim, can you show me a professional person who would help me to buy goods.” I said, “Yes, I can do so.” The narrator has said that a camel man asked me to speak on his behalf to abu Ja‘far (a.s.) to take part in certain matters of his affairs. I went to see him (abu Ja‘far (a.s.) to speak to him but he was having meal with a group of people and I did not get a chance to speak to him. He (abu Ja‘far (a.s.) said, “O abu Hashim, eat. He placed food before me. Then he said, initiating and without any question from me, “O slave, take good care of the camel-man that abu Hashim has brought for us. Keep him with you.” The narrator has said that one day I entered a garden along with him and said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, I am addicted to eating fig. Pray to Allah for me.” He was quite and then after three day on his own initiation he said, “O abu Hashim, “Allah has removed your addiction.” Ever since it is the thing that I hate most.”
